subject: Hosted API pricing bands & peak TPS — follow-up

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@metriclabs.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing bands & peak TPS — follow-up

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really appreciated the context on MetricLabs' streaming transcription workflow. Quick recap from my side and a couple of asks so we can get you a tailored pricing band.

Call recap (short):
- Primary workload: near-real-time transcription + short-context summarization (user sessions ~ 1–2 turns).
- Typical monthly volume: you mentioned mid-to-high double digits of millions of tokens, with spikes tied to batch processing windows.
- Peak behavior: brief spikes during scheduled ingestion windows; you said “high single to low triple-digit TPS range” for short periods.

Action items I need to finalize the hosted estimate:
1) Confirm expected steady-state monthly token volume (range OK).
2) Confirm peak TPS (requests/sec OR tokens/sec) and approximate duration of spikes.
3) Target $/1M tokens or target monthly budget range to aim price bands against.
4) Any special security/KMS or compliance requirements that would affect pricing (e.g., dedicated isolation, longer retention, audit logs).

If you can reply with the numbers above today or tomorrow, I’ll get a tailored workbook back to you (includes unit-econ lines for 1M/10M/100M tiers and a modeled SLA premium). I’ve attached a placeholder estimate workbook so you can see the fields we’ll populate: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (stub).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if that’s easier.

—

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@metriclabs.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands & peak TPS — follow-up

Hi Olga — thanks for the recap and the workbook. Answers below:

1) Steady-state monthly tokens: expecting ~90M tokens/month (we see a range, so provision for 80–130M is helpful).
2) Peak TPS: during ingestion windows we hit ~140 requests/sec for ~15–20 minutes; average tokens per request ~45, so peak token throughput ~6.3k tokens/sec during bursts.
3) Budget target: procurement has scoped $600–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on SLA/latency guarantees. If you can give two bands (standard vs low-latency) with calibrated unit economics, that’d be ideal.
4) Security: standard SOC2 controls are fine for now; we may need KMS in the procurement phase (procurement@metriclabs.com will handle legal/reqs).

Decision timeline: We’re aiming to select a vendor by end of this month; procurement loop-in will be next week.

Thanks — happy to review the workbook once you populate it.

Alicia
Senior Product Ops Manager
MetricLabs

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands & peak TPS — follow-up

Appreciate the quick numbers, Alicia — that helps a lot. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we finalize the workbook:

- Can you confirm percent split between streaming (long-lived streams) vs short request/response (chat-style)? We’ll treat streaming as more expensive in the unit model.
- Are the ingestion-window spikes predictable (scheduled batch runs) vs user-driven bursts? If scheduled, we can recommend burst credits vs sustained capacity.
- For the budget band: is the $600 number contingent on longer commitments / reserved capacity or is that on-the-table for hosted pay-as-you-go?

Next steps from our side: Marissa (CS) will draft a 3-tier pricing band (standard / low-latency / reserved) with modeled monthly cost at 80M / 100M / 130M token points and show effective $/1M and projected monthly total. Rishi will check if we need a specific KMS addon for procurement.

I’ll aim to get the populated workbook back to you by Wednesday afternoon PT. If procurement wants specific language, include procurement@metriclabs.com and we’ll attach the procurement packet and SOC2 evidence.

—
Olga
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted pricing bands — initial model (attached)

Hi Alicia / Olga — attaching an initial pricing workbook and a small CSV snapshot (metriclabs-volume-snapshot.csv) that maps your described traffic to costs. Attachment stubs: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx, metriclabs-volume-snapshot.csv.

Key unit-econ points from the model (high-level):
- Steady-state: 90M tokens/mo -> modeled effective price (standard hosted) = $1,020 per 1M tokens -> est monthly cost ≈ $91,800.
- With a 12‑month reserved commit (predictable 100M tokens/mo) we can target $680 per 1M tokens -> est monthly cost ≈ $68,000 (Reserved band).
- Low-latency (streaming optimized) band adds ~18% premium to the standard hosted price due to lower batching and higher SLOs.
- Burst handling: for 140 req/sec peaks (~6.3k tokens/sec) of ~20 minutes, recommended: keep hosted with burst credits (no infra change) OR move to Dedicated if sustained >30 min.

Notes / asks for you:
1) Confirm whether you want the Reserved band to assume a 12-month commit or 6-month commit (pricing differs).
2) Any additional compliance add-ons (KMS, extended audit logs) so I can add explicit line items.
3) If procurement wants, I can export a one-page cost comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a sample SLA clause for approval.

We’ll update the workbook with the exact numbers for the three tiers and send back by EOD Thursday PT.
